record.title: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
record.summary: Bhagtani et al. report ERPBench, a benchmark that grades screenshot-only computer-use agents against ground-truth ERPNext database state and separately tracks navigation, interaction, commit and database correctness. In the paper’s tested tasks, screen/form progress does not reliably imply a correct stored record; its abstract reports that some agents save in up to 85% of runs but write the correct value in as few as 3%. The authors report five independent runs per task under each configuration. This is a paper-reported benchmark result, not an independent reproduction or a claim about all enterprise agents.

evidence_gaps.description: The paper reports six agents across ERPNext tasks and uses a database grader as definitive task success. the research desk did not reproduce the runs or audit the full task corpus. Cheapest next step: inspect the released benchmark/tasks and independently rerun a matched subset with database-state grading.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, database-state grading exposes a reliability failure hidden by screen-level success in enterprise computer-use agents and can change evaluation practice; evidence is limited to one benchmark and its tested models/tasks.
limitations: Results are author-reported in one preprint and were not independently reproduced in this review.
The claims are limited to the paper’s stated benchmark tasks, agents and evaluation protocol; transfer to other workflows or benchmark families is unknown.
Code/artifacts and detailed appendices were not audited in this activation.

technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible preprint specifies the method and reports experiments; the research desk verified the claims in the paper but did not independently reproduce them.
technical.mechanism: The paper proposes and evaluates state-grounded scoring that checks post-run ERP database values and decomposes task progress into navigation, interaction, commit and database stages.
technical.regime: The paper’s author-reported ERPNext tasks, tested agents and five independent runs per task/configuration.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares against existing enterprise computer-use agents and human reference runs using a shared database grader.

brief.title: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
brief.why_it_matters: If the measured gap holds, evaluating persistent application state rather than screen-level completion can change how enterprise computer-use agents are tested and deployed. The claim is limited to this benchmark and its tested models/tasks.
